title: Seven proven keys to quickly close care gaps by upcoming HEDIS and CMS Stars deadlines
summary: Electronic health records integrations with genetic testing increases operational efficiency, enhances the provider experience and offers precision medicine at scale.
body_markdown:
### *Original publication date: September, 2025*


Closing care gaps in preventive screenings, chronic care management and other high-impact HEDIS measures is critical for health plans and providers to achieve optimal quality ratings and incentive payments. Whether you're managing a Medicare Advantage (MA) plan, a Medicaid MCO, a commercial population health program or an ACO, it can be especially stressful as the pressure to close gaps in care intensifies when HEDIS and CMS Stars deadlines approach.


When deadlines loom, healthcare organizations often grapple with:


1. Persistent care gaps
2. Member disengagement
3. Incomplete open orders
4. Provider capacity, fatigue or reluctance to act
5. Identifying fast, scalable interventions


However, it’s never too late to close gaps in care.


## Why closing care gaps now matters


The stakes are high. Failure to meet these HEDIS and CMS-Star-related targets and deadlines can have severe implications, including:


- Automatic 1-star rating reduction on measures with inaccurate or uncompliant data
- Potential drag on the overall Star rating, affecting public perception and competitiveness
- Loss of lucrative quality bonus payments for plans with fewer than 4 stars
- Potential enrollment sanctions or termination for consistently low-performing ratings
- Increased regulatory oversight and potential penalties


In contrast, improving scores can bring opportunities and drive both financial and clinical benefits.


Opportunities include:


- Plans experiencing a 1-star increase can see an[8%-12% enrollment boost](https://guidehouse.com/-/media/www/site/insights/healthcare/2018/medicare-advantage-analysis.pdf) the following year
- An increase from 3 to 4 stars can boost revenue by[$12-$16.2 million](https://www.healthleadersmedia.com/strategy/one-star-improvement-can-increase-medicare-advantage-revenue-17) for a 9,600-member health plan
- Medicare Shared Savings Programs[saved $5.2 billion,](https://www.qliqsoft.com/blog/the-financial-upside-of-closing-care-gaps-in-care) with $3.1 billion paid of those savings going to ACOs
- Meeting NCQA requirements necessary for many Medicaid state contracts
- Medicaid MCOs may receive financial incentives tied to quality benchmarks, and their contracts in some states may require improved quality performance to achieve NCQA accreditation
- MA plans with a 4-star rating or higher can receive up to a 5% quality bonus—representing approximately[$16 billion in additional revenue](https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=eeda99d4-aaaf-4981-acae-be264147e26c)


Beyond the financial implications, improving quality performance demonstrates a health plan's commitment to preventive care and better health outcomes for members.


Even if deadlines are near, there are still ways to quickly close gaps in care. Here are seven keys to making a fast, significant impact on your quality measures, patient care and—ultimately—your bottom line.


## Seven keys to closing gaps in care at the final stretch


**1. Meet members where they are**


Convenience is crucial when it comes to engaging your members quickly. With over 2,200 patient service center (PSC) locations—including Labcorp at Walgreens—we have sites within miles of 95% of the U.S. population. This gives your members unmatched access to complete lab testing locally.


Labcorp also has many FDA-cleared self-collection kits available for high-impact measures like colorectal cancer screening, diabetes control and kidney health evaluation to provide a convenient option for members who can’t or would prefer not to leave their home. These outreach options allow quick and easy access to diagnostic services for your members.


**2. Established payer integrations**


Experience is essential when it comes to supporting quality improvement campaigns close to HEDIS and CMS deadlines. Our established payer integrations via networks and API integration with major EHRs such as Epic, LINK and SFTP mean we can hit the ground running with your organization any time of year.


We worked with one large national health plan to[close their colorectal screening](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/how-labcorp-worked-large-national-plan-improve-member-health) gaps in care to more effectively improve their member health. *The results were 2.6 times higher return rates and follow-up.*


We have also seen impressive results from our late-year deployment campaigns:


**Case Study 1: MA Plan**


With just three months left in the measurement year, an MA plan was struggling with low colorectal cancer screening rates. Labcorp deployed a targeted FIT kit campaign using our multi-channel outreach and easy-to-use at-home collection kits.


As a result, the plan saw a 15% increase in screening compliance, pushing them over the threshold for a 4-star rating on this measure.


**Case Study 2: Medicaid MCO**


An MCO needed to improve their diabetes care measures but faced significant member disengagement. Labcorp implemented a combination of at-home A1c kits and targeted outreach to drive PSC visits for comprehensive diabetes panels.


With this campaign, the MCO achieved a 20% increase in diabetes care compliance, meeting state benchmarks and securing performance incentives.


By using our diagnostic reach, logistics capabilities and member engagement expertise, health plans can make measurable progress toward quality goals during the home stretch.


**3. Tailored program options for every population**


There’s no such thing as a one-size-fits-all gaps in care program. To maximize success, solutions must be tailored to the needs of your specific population.


Labcorp offers two managed programs and one coordinated gap closure solution that delivers customized outreach and reminders for your members and access to a reporting dashboard with key performance indicators, weekly activity files and HL7 data feeds.


**Two managed program options:**


Whether your population is highly engaged or requires more outreach, our opt-in and auto-deploy options offer the flexibility to meet your members where they are—requiring minimal lift from your internal team.


**Opt-in**


- Members self-enroll online and submit their test specimen through collection at one of more than 2,200 PSCs across the U.S. or using an at-home collection kit
- Seamless registration-to-results in Labcorp Patient™ portal
- Includes email and text reminders, kit tracking and access to digital results
- 2024 kit return rate: 58.8%


**Auto-deploy**


- Members can be pre-identified by you or we can identify those in need using our database of lab results for testing performed by Labcorp
- Labcorp mails test collection kits to identified members
- Results are available via mail and the member’s Labcorp Patient™ account
- Includes step-by-step instructions in English and Spanish, reminders and Labcorp customer care team support
- 97.5% customer satisfaction
- 2024 kit return rate: 16.5%


**Coordinated program**


Our coordinated gaps in care program is a flexible option ideal for fully-integrated health plans, ACOs and TPA partners that use physicians as the ordering provider with strong in-house outreach capabilities that want to maintain existing workflows while adding convenient at-home collection testing access for members.


**Labcorp’s coordinated program gives you:**


- Flexibility to customize program delivery to your operations and support your population health strategy
- Streamlined results-sharing with ordering and primary care providers
- Proven CLIA-certified lab accuracy, reliability and service support
- The ability for an authorized in-network provider to order each test, simplifying fulfillment and accelerating deployment


**4. Rapid turnaround times**


Diagnostics companies need a robust logistics infrastructure to offer fast shipping and turnaround times. Because when it comes to member health and your quality measure performance, every member and every minute counts.


With a large, national footprint, Labcorp processes more than 3 million patient specimens every week and is equipped to deliver your members’ results promptly.


Labcorp's turnaround time for test results depends on the type of test being performed.


**Standard routine tests** (Complete blood count (CBC), basic metabolic panel, cholesterol, etc.)


- Typical turnaround: 1 to 3 business days


**Specialty or esoteric tests** (Complex genetic, molecular or send-out tests)


- Typical turnaround: 3 to 7 business days


**At-home collection kits** (FIT, A1c, etc.)


- Kits are shipped to your member within 3 to 5 business days of sending us your mailing files
- Members typically receive results within 3 to 5 business days after Labcorp receives member sample
- Members can access their results 24 hours a day seven days a week in the Labcorp Patient Portal™


**Rapid tests** (COVID-19 PCR, flu, etc.)


- Turnaround often within 24–48 hours after Labcorp receives member sample


This level of rapid response is especially helpful as HEDIS and Star submission deadlines are right around the corner.


**5. Data-driven insights and integration**


Effectively[leveraging lab data](https://www.labcorp.com/leveraging-lab-data-combat-diabetes-and-chronic-kidney-disease) to manage chronic diseases like diabetes, chronic kidney disease and colorectal cancer has become crucial for payers and providers. The right data and analytics help facilitate gap closure and support clinical decision making.


Complement your care management and home visits with Labcorp’s expansive data and analytic insights, with our standardized data set including more than 45 billion lab results—50% of the U.S. population. Get access to:


- Analytics that stratify populations and identify rising-risk members
- Targeted interventions to drive preventive screenings and close care gaps
- Support for risk adjustment through comprehensive lab data
- Data identifying members who’ve already closed a gap so you can engage them throughout their healthcare journey to maximize plan investments
- Actionable insights to track program performance and inform optimizations at the program, population and individual levels with our real-time analytics


Beyond closing gaps, Labcorp's diagnostic insights can help health plans optimize[coding for value-based care success,](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/how-lab-data-enables-more-accurate-patient-coding-value-based-care-success) risk adjustment and quality measure performance—all factors that influence incentive payments and Star ratings for MA plans.


A standardized framework for healthcare data exchange increases speed, consistency and uniformity across different systems and simplifies the process of analyzing claims data to identify gaps in care to support easier and more efficient HEDIS reporting. Efficient exchange of large volumes of claims data and enhanced analytics through our HL7 claims feeds can result in[reduced costs of up to $30 billion](https://www.suretysystems.com/insights/hl7-integration-unlocking-the-key-benefits-and-challenges/#:~:text=healthcare%20costs%20of%20up%20to%20%2430%20billion%2C,facilitate%20data%20exchange%20between%20various%20healthcare%20systems) in national healthcare expenses due to improved interoperability and the ability to facilitate data exchange between various healthcare systems.


Our reporting also meets quality measure data requirements, making it easier for you to submit accurate and complete information.


**6. Member-centric, multi-channel engagement**


A member-centric approach is critical to improving their engagement. Labcorp prioritizes the member experience by offering:


- Multilingual support
- Pre-notification and reminder communications
- Easy-to-understand educational content that resonates with members
- Multi-channel outreach tailored to each population (mail, email, text)
- Labcorp clinicians call members directly in the case of abnormal results
- For managed programs, a customer care team is available from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. EST to support members with questions
- Co-branding opportunities to reinforce health plan partnership and leverage the trust you’ve built with them to increase engagement


Our multi-channel outreach capabilities allow us to educate members in ways that resonate best, driving awareness and activation.


**7. Regulatory compliance**


Implementing gap closure programs can come with a complex web of laws and regulations to navigate. Our multi-channel outreach strategy has been designed to adhere to HIPAA, TCPA, CMS guidelines and more, giving you peace of mind about compliance.


This includes but is not limited to:


- HIPAA privacy and security measures
- TCPA rules on automated calls and text messages
- CMS and state regulations on any communications dealing with MA, Medicaid, commercial Medicare Part D plans
- State laws that are more stringent than federal laws, such as New York, California, Florida and others
- Required messages tailored to Medicare members and those with limited English proficiency as well as accessible communications for visually impaired members


Labcorp also handles consent management, audit trails, data segmentation, vendor oversight and more, freeing your staff up to focus on your strategic initiatives.


**Measurable results when it matters most**


Labcorp has demonstrated an ability to drive positive quality measure results, including:


- 17.1% return rate for a home collection colorectal cancer screening program launched in Q4
- Doubled the diabetes control testing rate for an MA plan in just eight weeks
- 97.5% customer satisfaction for members using our at-home collection services
- 95%+ 2024 Payer CSAT Score
- 50 2024 Payer Net Promoter Score (in the excellent category)


## Comprehensive solutions aligned to quality incentives

Our solutions are tailored to address the unique needs of health plans and providers when time is tight. With Labcorp, you get access to end-to-end services without the administrative burdens that typically emerge for in-house gap closure programs—especially valuable when the end of the year is approaching.
